Today I lost phase 1 of my bet with @ercwl.

I was calling ETH to $500 and it only dropped to like $890.

Phase 2 of our bet expires ~June 2024. If ETH hasn't dropped by $500 by then, Eric keeps the cube. If it has, he sends it back to me.

I'm a little bit relieved he already had the cube made up and it only cost me 1 million sats.

Since the surprise is no longer relevant, I'll spill the beans on what I was doing.

I had actually commissioned bitcoin artist @asanoha_gold to make a 1/1 gold edged masterpiece on a 4" tungsten cube that weighed ~40 lbs.

Each side of this cube was going to be inscribed with a unique bitcoin block from each of the first 4 epochs of Bitcoin:

Epoch 1: Genesis Block
Epoch 2: Block 210,000 first halving
Epoch 3: Block 505,225 First 2MB block, after segwit
Epoch 4: Block 774,628 First 4MB inscription block, after taproot

If I was going to lose the bet, I wanted to lose the bet in style. I wanted to give a 1/1 physical piece of art that would represent Bitcoin.

The artist and myself are very much against BRC20 spam and the strawmannirg & negative things the ordinals leaders say about bitcoin monetary maximalists all the time - so we were very torn on honouring the 4MB block.

I decided to put aside my personal feelings and recognize the 4MB block for what it was - a piece of art. 

The first 4 MB inscription block is infamous, it was a political statement and a unique & influential piece of graffiti in Bitcoin's history.

Every 4 MB inscription block after it is just stupid.

Even still - the artist and myself were torn, and debated the merits of continuing down this path as the last week or 2 of the inscriptions debacle seemed to get more and more contentious.

In the end this thing was going to cost me about $15,000 to make. We were just placing the order for the cube this week.

I'm a little bit relieved that Eric had already made up a small cheap one that matches his motif of lost bets, because we couldn't really bring ourselves to spend that much time, money & energy into honoring that 4MB block.

However, this concept of gold wrapped tungsten cubes representing important bitcoin blocks is pretty sticky. 

Asanoha and I might make a series of these as a limited edition of 21 cubes, we will likely replace the 4MB block with block 823129, the first @ocean_mining block that was mined with the standard template that filters spam.
